verdicts.note: Attacked toward -2 and toward 0. She is the appointed incumbent (S1, S3) running on the training and modernization she has done since February (S1, S4), so the proven-record side is right. Her tenure is eight months and she has never been elected, which keeps it at -1 rather than -2.

S4 ('strong internal controls, improving efficiency and ensuring transparency') and S2 ('Every Dollar Accounted For'; treats tax dollars 'like her own') both fit pole_a's oversight and restraint. She proposes no new programs. Two sources, so medium holds; nothing in the dossier points toward expansion.

Never held office (S1, S3) and runs on 'something is broken in the Auditor's office' (S1). +1 rather than +2 is reasonable: his pitch is professional finance expertise, not generational change or outsider energy as such. It is consistent with Park at -1.

Actual-to-budget reporting, a KPI dashboard and quarterly updates (S4), plus 10-day financial disclosure (S6), are the oversight and performance standards pole_a describes. His wish to help departments 'prioritize spending' (S4) is about allocation, not expansion, so it does not pull toward pole_b.
